expectedLaw.L1-totality: Same kind: the dependency position for primary partition P (subjects X) is supported only when exact (dependency relation, rung, S) partitions paired to the evidence jointly contain every x in X. Reason: RC-4 ties the primary relation's claim to the dependency 'over the same examined set'; a folded complete dependency entry backed by a strict subset of X is a fictional complete entry for the uncovered subjects; native step 1 answers an absent dependency with required-relation-missing.
expectedLaw.L2-uncovered-subject: If some x in X lies in no paired dependency partition, no completeness-dependent value may rest on that dependency: the result must be unknown with coverage-unknown at S and required-relation-missing in nativeDeficiencies, i.e. the same answer as having no dependency partition at all. No new cause token is needed.
expectedLaw.L3-dominance: Known matches and exceeded count bounds are unaffected (completeness-only change).
expectedLaw.L4-disjoint: Lawful disjoint dependency partitions {f} and {g} satisfy totality; the fold then decides, and complete evidence gives true, order independent.
expectedLaw.L5-overlap: Overlapping same-partitionKey dependency scopes are refused at close_run (SUBJECT_SCOPE_PARTITION_OVERLAP); at the atom API they are a synthetic shape only and carry no law.
expectedLaw.L6-outgoing: Outgoing X = {subject}; any paired partition containing the subject already satisfies totality; no outgoing answer should change.
expectedLaw.L7-empty-X: X empty: totality is vacuous, but 'containing those native ids' pairs nothing, so the dependency is absent and the answer is unknown. That is conservative, not unsound; whether an explicit empty dependency scope should close an empty primary partition is not stated by any owner (under-specified, conservative).
expectedLaw.L8-whole-source: Different kind (clones->declares) and attestation views use 'whole-source search of (S, T)'. No owner states whether the whole-source dependency must cover S's dependency-kind population; the reference folds whatever partitions exist. Expected: genuinely under-specified; flag, do not claim a defect.
expectedLaw.L9-reachability: Not excluded at close_run (disjointness only; no omission row for calls/reachability) nor at admit_coverage_result_v3 (one scope, one entry; cannot see calls). The execution-inputs census makes a REQUIRED calls cell's account incomplete and the Run indeterminate, which neutralizes the Run verdict but not the atom value inside proof; an OPTIONAL calls cell carries no required deficiency. Expected: no owner admission exclusion; not demonstrated as a full Run.

expectedClassification: source35 incoming partial-dependency answer (all-covered true) is a REFERENCE DEFECT against L1/L2 as derived from RC-4 + no-fictional-complete-entries + native step 1, with textual under-specification at the atom dependency sentence ('containing those native ids' does not say 'every'); the empty-X and whole-source boundaries are under-specified, not defects.
candidateSmallestRemedy: In _select_dep_coverages, same-kind branch: after pairing exact scopes that contain any current subject, if the union of the paired scopes' subjects does not contain every current subject, return no partitions (the dependency occupies no position). Contract sentence: 'pair dep Coverage to exact current-source scopes; the paired scopes must jointly contain every current source subject, otherwise the dependency contributes no position.'
